questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First, I wanted to go as far away as possible to a destination that I would like to visit for the culture, the sights and the nature, but was difficult to visit due to the distance and price. Secondly, I wanted to go to an English-speaking country in order to practice my own English skills and be able to understand the lecturers most efficiently. A third aspect was that I wanted to go a high ranked university with courses that I find interesting, in order to get the most out of the courses. Especially within neuroscience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad experience was really good. Canada is an amazing country; the people are kind, and the nature is extraordinary as well as some of the bigger cities. There was a lot to experience around in Canada, however Hamilton, the city where the university is located is quite boring. There is not much to do in the city except studying so you will have to travel away during weekends and reading week in order to get the most out of the study abroad experience. The study program and social life was good as well. So, after all I was happy to go abroad. However, i would have wished that the city was a bit more interesting with more things to do in the city. I compensated from that from travelling a lot, which was a bit expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: That was really easy. McMaster provided me with several mails and an app that that explained everything you need to know

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got the mails describing what to do. In addition to that there was an introductory meeting explaining all relevant things as well. And the people working at the university was happy to show me around and helping me out. In addition to that we had a whole day where our exchange buddies showed us around campus and answered all our questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was quite difficult compared to what I was told by previous students at McMaster. We talked to several landlords who explained that the covid19 situation really affected the wish to rent out basements or rooms. Several facebook groups exist, however many of them is mostly spam or scams. A lot of people that you get in contact with would want to receive a deposit before even showing the apartment, which you should not do. Some people in the facebook groups are however legit, so you should apply to become part of these groups. You could also have luck finding an apartment of Kijiji (their version of DBA) or
roomies.ca
. A recommendation could also be to write to apartments on airBNB to hear if they would be interested in renting out the apartment for the whole period. Often they are willing to do so at a cheaper price than the one listed, since airBNB charge a fee themselves.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You should find accommodation in the area around campus called Westdale or Ainslee wood. Downtown Hamilton is bit sketchy with a lot of homeless people and addicts and there is really nothing to do there. Most things happens on campus. However living off campus is much more cheaper than living on campus. And when living on Campus you are forced to by their meal plan so you will be eating at restaurants/school cafe all the time. The people living on campus is also mostly 1. Year students, meaning that they are 17-18 years old, so you might not have that much in common. 

When living off campus, you are probably going to stay at a big old house, so you might want to find a group of people to apply with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process itself was easy. You got a mail with a link to an application to fill out and they you got another mail later with acceptance and a step by step guide for what to do know. However when enrolling in courses, there was some issues. There platform made it easy to see which courses to choose or if any overlapped. But when trying to enroll, it said that you did not meet the prerequisites, since we did not pass any of the McMaster courses required, so I had to text the academic advisor to get approval, so some of the courses was filled up before I was able to enroll.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got several mails informing me what to do. You could also get help by writing to the academic advisor, but she answered a bit slow. I ended up just showing up to a course I wanted and told her to help me register for the course, so I was enrolled the day after.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Many of the courses I wanted overlapped, but I ended up having my 1., 2., 3. and 18th priority

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for the courses as soon as registration opens. The courses will be available to look at 3 days prior to the day registration opens. You might already look at the courses at that point and write to academic advisor immediately to get confirmation of prerequisites, since it may take a while and courses fill up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was pretty much like the level at University of Copenhagen. However, it was much more easier to receive good grades and the expectations was much more lower than was we are used to. In addition to that, there was no books or articles to read. The syllabus was only what was told during lectures and what appeared on the slides.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching varied a bit compared to UCPH. The lectures were pretty much what we are used to. However, the only thing we did during tutorials were presentations, so we didn't learn to use the knowledge we acquired during lectures. Also, they had some quizzes, assignments and presentations which all was part of our final grade together with participation points and midterms. Despite it sounds like a lot, it was fairly easy to get done in no time and it was nice to already having completed most of the final grade before the final exams. Most exams was already passed before even going to the exam, due to all of the other components. All the exams I had was for 2 hours written exams with a combination of multiple choice and short answer questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LIFESCI 3BB3 Neurobiology of Disease
BIOCHEM 4E03 Gene Regulation in Stem Cells and Development
HTHSCI 3K03 Principles of virology
MOLBIOL 3O03 Microbial Genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend Principles of Virology. By far the best course in my opinion. The professor was really really good, the topics was really interesting and her way of quizzing and examination was really fair. Instead of a midterm, we had 3 quizzes covering 5-7 lectures each, so really manageable to prepare for. 
I would also recommend Neurobiology of Disease. I am really interested in neuroscience, so I found this course really interesting. The professor is good and 40% of the grade is a community engagement project where you have to work on an assignment/scientific article and creative media to explain a disease which one of the university community partners is associated with (Epilepsy, addiction or Autism).
Gene regulation in stem cells and development was a exciting course as well, despite the first lectures was rather unimportant. The professor was really good at explaining the concepts, however he was a bit arrogant and frustrating and it seemed like he didn't really want to do the lectures. This course was the only one we had which were online for some reason and there were no tutorials at all.
Microbial genetics I would not recommend. The lecture concepts didn't really interest me at all and her way of testing was really unfair. It was much about applying the knowledge we received during lectures, however we didn't learn to apply it since tutorials were all about presenting scientific papers. However the professor her self was good at explaining the concepts during lectures, but wasn't really the things we were taught that we were examined in. 
Also I started out having Neuroscience of learning and memory, however I had to switch course since the professor had a thick accent which were impossible to understand and there was to much group work to be done, which I tried to avoid since we spend most weekends travelling.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: All the prices that you see everywhere is without tax, so you have to multiply the amount with 13% in order to get the real price and even more if the product contains sugar. You also have to pay 15%-22% tips everywhere, both at the hairdresser, bar and every restaurants, otherwise you might be yelled at…

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices are much like the danish prices, except for the fact that you have to pay tax and tips, so it becomes more expensive. Fast food is really expensive as well. Soda is much more cheaper than we are used. And domestic flights and flights to the USA is really cheap as well. Skiing however is really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of clubs that you could be part of. There was a gym, swimming pool, squash courts and table tennis tables free of charge. You could also create your own sports team in almost every sport you can think of and play against other teams at the university. McMaster also have a Canadian football team that was free to watch play every Sunday. The university also showed all the world cup soccer games and held bonfires and barbeques occasionally. They also planned several trips out of the city to national parks, Ikea and other things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Create a sports team together with the other exchange students, show up to club fest if you want to be part of club and go on the moose trip for exchange students before the start of semester. That is where you will get most of your friendships started.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
My biggest recommendation is to go to Banff and Jasper National Park either before the start of the semester or during reading week for the midterms. That is the most beautiful place i have ever seen. However, look out for when lake Moraine and the Maligne lake cruise closes for the season, since these two places are must see together with lake Louise. These national parks are also exceptional for wildlife spotting (moose, elk and bears) and for stargazing since it is a night sky reserve. You can eventually combine this trip with a trip to Vancouver (amazing city as well as Vancouver Island) and then rent a car and go to whistler (for bungee jumping and trekking).

You should go to Toronto to see the city and some of the typical Canadian/American sports eg. ice hockey and basketball. I also went to see baseball and soccer as well. McMaster has a Canadian football team as well playing every Sunday with free admission to the stands. 

I also recommend going to Montreal for the weekend to see the city. Niagara Falls is a must see as well. We also rented a car and drove to Algonquin park for the weekend, which was pretty nice, especially during fall to see the Indian summer (google when to go!). Flights to New york was also pretty cheap and so was flights to Boston, Washington or Miami. I also went skiing in Whistler after the exams, which were a bucket list thing for me to do. It was nice, but not worth the cost of it in my opinion (it cost 10.000 dkk for 4 days of skiing without food and flights).

Also make sure you are home for homecoming. +10.000 people meet up in the street for partying all day

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: That was really easy. However most Canadian at the university was pretty young and we didn't get to talk that much with locals. We almost only spoke with the other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is difficult to get to socialize with the local students. It seems like they don't do much except studying. However you could apply for a sports team as a free agent, you could try to group up with locals when doing group work or go to house parties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find anything challenging when it comes to the cultural differences. except for the thing with their way of paying tips for almost everything

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their culture is much like ours, so it is easy to adapt. Also the Canadians in general are really friendly and they are committed to the university sport teams which is nice and most people walk around in university merch.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on the Moose trip before start of the semester, this is the best way to get friends. 

Plan going out of the city in the weekends. Hamilton is a boring city, however Canada has a lot of amazing places that you must see. Especially the West coast - Banff and Jasper. 

Try to do good on your quizzes, presentations and assignment, that way you dont have a lot of pressure in the end and have more time to explore Canada, since you already might have passed your courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apparently the east coast of Canada is not that cold. We had +20 degrees in november, however the week after it was snowing, so pack clothes for all weathers. Also Canada is more expensive that you might think, so save up or apply for legacies.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definatly the friendships and the travelling to amazing cities and nature around in Canada.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing was a bit anoying, since i started living in hotels and airBNBs for the first 1,5 week for 1000 DKK a night.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
